methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two sets of information.
mindtraced_atomic_units: FSM acts as an arbiter for three requesting devices (r[1], r[2], r[3])
Resetn is an active-low synchronous reset to state A
FSM stays in state A when no requests are present (r[1]=0, r[2]=0, r[3]=0)
If r[1]=1 in state A, transition to B (g[1]=1)
If r[1]=0 and r[2]=1 in state A, transition to C (g[2]=1)
If r[1]=0, r[2]=0, and r[3]=1 in state A, transition to D (g[3]=1)
If r[1]=0, r[2]=0, and r[3]=0 in state A, stay in A
If r[1]=1 in state B, stay in B
If r[1]=0 in state B, transition to A
If r[2]=1 in state C, stay in C
If r[2]=0 in state C, transition to A
If r[3]=1 in state D, stay in D
If r[3]=0 in state D, transition to A
Verilog code should use separate always blocks for state table and flip-flops
FSM outputs g[i] should be described using continuous assignment or always block
State codes can be assigned freely
spec_atomic_units: Module implements an FSM arbiter for three devices
Clock input clk, active-low reset resetn, 3-bit request input r, 3-bit grant output g
Priority: device 1 > device 2 > device 3
State transitions occur on rising edge of clk
Resetn resets FSM to state A synchronously
r inputs sampled on rising edge of clk
g outputs reflect current state, updated synchronously with clock
Critical path: r inputs -> combinational logic -> next state register setup
Resetn asserted long enough before clk rising edge for proper reset
g timing depends on clock-to-output delay and combinational logic delay
FSM implemented with two always blocks: state flip-flops and state transition logic
State flip-flops use non-blocking assignments
State transition logic uses combinational always block
State register stores current state
Next state determined by current state and r inputs
g outputs assigned based on current state
One register for the state register
